scope: Scientific source/document qualification of the 44-project census. Inputs/outputs are proposed adapter contracts; only statements in evidence findings are claims about inspected software. Acceptance tests and restrictions are proposed, not executed adapters or runtime qualification.
version_policy: Observed package versions and README/source bytes are independent observations unless a source URL pins a commit. Hashes identify inspected bytes; a commit-pinned API is not automatically the published package release.

projects.input: A named observed/latent graph, intervention variables, outcome and target population.
projects.output: An identification expression, or a recorded identification failure; estimation is a separate operation.
projects.assumptions: The supplied graph and intervention semantics are substantively justified; the selected identification algorithm applies to its graph class.
projects.adapter_rule: Keep graph and expression identities. A successful identify_effect call does not imply an available estimator for its returned expression. Do not reinterpret an unsupported expression as nonidentification.
projects.acceptance_test: Use adjustment, front-door and nonidentified latent-IV witnesses; independently evaluate supported expressions on finite laws and verify unsupported-estimator status.

evidence.finding: identify_effect selects IDIdentifier for id-algorithm; estimate_effect requires a separate method and identified estimand.

projects.role: Heterogeneous effects and dynamic moment estimation
projects.input: Outcome, treatment, controls, heterogeneity features and estimator-specific IV or equal-length trajectory groups.
projects.output: A selected CATE or structural blip coefficient with its model-specific inference object.
projects.assumptions: Exchangeability or valid-IV assumptions, residual relevance, specified treatment-response form, and independent/dependent sampling assumptions appropriate to the selected estimator.
projects.adapter_rule: For inspected DynamicDML, sort and validate actual periods, require equal group lengths and group-aware splitting, restrict heterogeneity features to baseline. Reject nontrivial sample_weight or sample_var because fit warns and ignores both. Do not pad missing periods without an observation model.
projects.acceptance_test: Permute rows then reconstruct chronological groups and obtain equivalent inputs; reject duplicate/missing periods and unsupported weights. Compare the backward blip solution with a finite linear oracle.

evidence.finding: Equal-length groups, occurrence-order periods, baseline heterogeneity, group-aware CV; weights and sample variance ignored.

projects.input: Outcome, treatment, covariates, optional instruments and explicit cluster variables; separate static or staggered-adoption panel schema.
projects.output: Specified score-model coefficient and inference; data containers alone return no causal effect.
projects.assumptions: The selected PLR/PLIV/IRM/IIVM or panel score matches the identified target, nuisance rates and sampling structure.
projects.adapter_rule: Do not treat DoubleMLPanelData as an arbitrary trajectory container. Default static_panel=False treats d as first-treatment timing; constructor permits only one treatment column. Distinguish clustered scores from general time-series inference and explicitly list adjustment columns.
projects.acceptance_test: Round-trip treatment-date and static-treatment examples without target change; reject two treatment columns and mixed cohort/action encoding. Compare a selected orthogonal score with its finite-law remainder and cluster-level splitting.

evidence.finding: Model families, fit, bootstrap, confidence intervals and tuning.
Data roles and cluster_cols belong to DoubleMLData.
Long-format panel semantics, static_panel default and single-treatment restriction.

projects.input: Experimental or observational (X,T,Y) with a separately established causal design.
projects.output: Method-specific heterogeneous-effect predictions used as inputs to targeting analysis.
projects.assumptions: Exchangeability, support and treatment consistency; CATE estimation and policy evaluation have separate accuracy and uncertainty requirements.
projects.adapter_rule: Limit the current qualification to the documented CATE/uplift role and benchmark facilities. Preserve method/target definitions; do not certify a policy from uplift ranking alone. Detailed method APIs require additional inspection before implementation.
projects.acceptance_test: Evaluate effect calibration and held-out policy value under known heterogeneous effects and a confounded challenger; separate treatment-response prediction from causal ranking.

evidence.finding: CATE/uplift purpose, experimental API warning and benchmark dataset/metric declarations.

projects.input: Numeric X,Y,W, nuisance predictions, optional sampling weights and clusters.
projects.output: Binary-treatment CATE; for continuous W the documented local covariance/variance coefficient, with selected forest uncertainty.
projects.assumptions: Unconfounded treatment and support; forest regularity and sampling assumptions; a continuous-treatment projection is not automatically a pointwise dose derivative.
projects.adapter_rule: Preserve equalize.cluster.weights and sample.weights as target metadata. Equalization requires sample.weights=NULL. Record honesty and ci.group.size; the latter must be at least two for interval computation.
projects.acceptance_test: Two clusters of sizes 1 and 9 with effects 0 and 10 distinguish cluster mean 5 from unit mean 9; verify target metadata and weighted aggregation. Compare continuous-treatment projection with a nonlinear dose derivative.

evidence.finding: Binary/continuous estimands, sample/cluster weights, honesty, interval group size and seeds.

projects.role: Temporal graph equivalence and graph-based effects
projects.input: Time series, declared lag window, masks, background knowledge, discovery method and conditional-independence test.
projects.output: Method-specific directed/undirected lag graph, time-series CPDAG or PAG; effects additionally require an assumed graph.
projects.assumptions: Method-specific stationarity and hidden-variable conditions; CI-test family matches distribution and dependence; an observed mask does not itself justify missingness.
projects.adapter_rule: Retain every endpoint, lag, test, window and method. PCMCI+, LPCMCI and regime variants are different model classes. A p-value matrix is not an effect estimate.
projects.acceptance_test: Use an autocorrelated confounded VAR and an observationally equivalent orientation example; assess graph-class coverage and admissible effect sets separately from edge F1.

evidence.finding: Explicit method assumptions/output classes, CI-test assumptions and declared features.

projects.input: Sample-by-feature data, CI test, significance level, background knowledge and FCI search limits.
projects.output: FCI GeneralGraph flagged as PAG plus edge-property objects.
projects.assumptions: Causal Markov/faithfulness and test assumptions; latent/selection semantics of FCI; finite samples do not turn uncertain endpoints into oriented arrows.
projects.adapter_rule: Serialize tails, arrowheads, circles, bidirected and undirected edges without collapsing to Boolean adjacency. Retain depth/max_path_length and distinguish restricted search from a full oracle result.
projects.acceptance_test: Round-trip all FCI endpoint pairs; verify an o-> edge stays unresolved and a bidirected edge stays distinct from two directed edges. Apply effect identification over compatible graphs.

evidence.finding: FCI input/output documentation, endpoint integer codes, search controls and graph.set_pag(True).

projects.input: No scientifically qualified interface in this source audit.
projects.output: No supported operation assigned.
projects.assumptions: A readable primary technical artifact is required before judging capabilities or current maintenance.
projects.adapter_rule: Defer dependency selection. Repository-access failures establish retrieval failure only; they do not prove abandonment or archive status.
projects.acceptance_test: Before evaluation, recover a licensed primary technical version, verify identity and inspect actual graph/estimation contracts.

evidence.finding: Repository retrieval failure only; no technical support.

projects.role: Joint graph and mechanism research comparator
projects.input: Observational variables and an additive-noise structural model with a graph prior/variational family.
projects.output: A fitted graph distribution and neural mechanisms; intervention simulation yields model-conditional ATE/CATE.
projects.assumptions: Structural ANM/noise/prior restrictions, sufficient causal information and adequate variational/optimization approximation.
projects.adapter_rule: Record structural priors and graph uncertainty. The current README says Rhino and DDECI were removed and points to v0.0.0; do not advertise temporal or latent-ADMG implementations from their cited papers alone.
projects.acceptance_test: Use Gaussian observational equivalence and non-Gaussian identifiable cases; distinguish data information from prior-driven orientation. Verify the exact installed release exposes each proposed model.

evidence.finding: DECI model, simulation, known-graph option and removed extensions.

projects.input: Method-specific sample data or event sequences, prior constraints and selected algorithm.
projects.output: Learned structure and graph comparison metrics for that method.
projects.assumptions: IID/function/score restrictions differ by algorithm; Hawkes/event-sequence models are separate from static ANMs.
projects.adapter_rule: Pin the gcastle submodule and backend. Its README labels HPCI under development; a monorepo push does not qualify it. Preserve graph equivalence where required and separate metric computation from identification.
projects.acceptance_test: Compare static ANM and event-sequence inputs using valid/invalid model assignments; reject routing generic time series to an IID algorithm without a declared reduction.

evidence.finding: Version declaration, algorithm categories, HPCI status, dependencies and PC example.

projects.input: Data and a linear/nonlinear structural loss with sparsity and acyclicity controls.
projects.output: A numerically optimized weighted DAG candidate.
projects.assumptions: Causal sufficiency and functional/noise identifiability separately from the log-determinant acyclicity construction.
projects.adapter_rule: Preserve optimization tolerance, threshold and seed; optimization feasibility and graph acyclicity are numerical statements, not evidence for causal orientation.
projects.acceptance_test: Check acyclicity before/after thresholding and compare equivalent Gaussian orientations; vary initialization and report target-effect sensitivity.

evidence.finding: DAGMA log-determinant/M-matrix formulation and linear/nonlinear usage.

projects.input: Data, regression loss, sparsity and numerical convergence/threshold choices.
projects.output: Estimated adjacency under an acyclicity constraint.
projects.assumptions: Graph interpretation needs structural/noise identifiability and valid observations beyond a differentiable DAG constraint.
projects.adapter_rule: Expose solver failure and thresholding; preserve pre-threshold weights. Do not label every fitted acyclic graph uniquely identified.
projects.acceptance_test: Use a cyclic near-threshold candidate, equivalent linear-Gaussian DAGs and a nonlinear identifiable case; compare feasibility with intervention correctness.

evidence.finding: Continuous constrained structure-learning formulation and reference code usage.

projects.input: A chosen discovery search and its test/score/data schema; exact search API still requires inspection.
projects.output: Search-specific graph through Java library/GUI or a separately pinned language bridge.
projects.assumptions: Each search retains its own equivalence class, latent-variable and sampling restrictions.
projects.adapter_rule: Do not count a Java repository snapshot as a qualified Python adapter. Pin tetrad-lib, bridge and JDK; README currently names JDK25+ and describes bridge installation as nonstandard.
projects.acceptance_test: For a selected FCI/PC route, compare oracle graph endpoints with the Python reference and require lossless cross-language graph serialization.

evidence.finding: Java model/GUI separation, Python/R bridges and runtime requirements; no selected search implementation inspected.

projects.input: A treated outcome series, a pre/post intervention split and unaffected control series.
projects.output: Posterior counterfactual series and intervention contrasts conditional on the structural time-series model.
projects.assumptions: Controls are unaffected by treatment; the pre-period outcome/control relation extends to the untreated post-period and competing shocks are accounted for.
projects.adapter_rule: Register donor/control exposure and the intervention date. Do not interpret posterior predictive fit or interval width as a test of no spillovers or stable counterfactual extrapolation.
projects.acceptance_test: Simulate a known campaign shock, then contaminate controls and introduce a post-period coefficient break; check model-conditional effects and failure diagnostics.

evidence.finding: Structural time-series target, unaffected-control and stable-relationship assumptions.

projects.input: A named quasi-experimental design, formula, timing/threshold variables and chosen Bayesian or OLS model.
projects.output: Design-specific contrast and posterior/OLS summaries; e.g. a local discontinuity at a supplied threshold.
projects.assumptions: Design-specific continuity, parallel-trend, donor or IV restrictions; prior and likelihood assumptions for Bayesian summaries.
projects.adapter_rule: Treat RD, DiD, synthetic control and IV as separate operations. Pin sampler/runtime configuration; the inspected README warns optional nutpie changes sampling defaults. Do not infer unconditional frequentist coverage from an HDI.
projects.acceptance_test: For a specified RD, recover the population jump under continuity and expose manipulation/discontinuity confounding; replay with an explicit sampler selection and check numerical diagnostics.

evidence.finding: Quasi-experimental methods, Bayesian/OLS outputs, runtime notes and RD example.

projects.input: Panel or IV/system regression data with explicit formula, effects, instruments and covariance choice.
projects.output: Linear model coefficients, residuals and model-specific covariance/diagnostics.
projects.assumptions: Strict exogeneity or stated IV moments; rank and dependence assumptions appropriate to each estimator.
projects.adapter_rule: Keep fixed effects, instrument sets and covariance axes explicit. The panel label does not establish dynamic-panel GMM support or a modern staggered-adoption ATT.
projects.acceptance_test: Compare within and IV estimates to direct projections on a small full-rank design, then use a lagged-outcome short panel to expose invalid strict-exogeneity routing.

evidence.finding: PanelOLS, first differences, IV2SLS/LIML/GMM and systems feature/usage descriptions.

projects.role: Python high-dimensional fixed-effect and panel candidate
projects.input: Formula-based outcomes, treatments, high-dimensional effects, weights, instruments and selected DiD/inference method.
projects.output: Selected regression or event-study effect and declared covariance.
projects.assumptions: The chosen regression/DiD estimand is identified; weights and dependence model match the target.
projects.adapter_rule: Do not convert a staggered-treatment request automatically into TWFE. Pin CPU/GPU backend and demeaning tolerances; declared speed/features are not this project's measured performance.
projects.acceptance_test: Recover a projection with explicit dummy variables; use heterogeneous cohort effects to distinguish TWFE from cohort ATT; compare weighted residualization and cluster covariance.

evidence.finding: FE/IV/GLM and DiD features, inference choices and backend declarations.

projects.input: Formula, multiple effects, optional instruments, weights and covariance specification.
projects.output: Linear/GLM or IV coefficients with selected inference.
projects.assumptions: Scientific regression/IV restrictions and weighting target are established outside formula parsing.
projects.adapter_rule: Retain formula expansion, absorbed effects, observations dropped and inference defaults. Benchmark claims cannot be transferred across hardware or a different estimand.
projects.acceptance_test: Check explicit-dummy equivalence, treatment collinearity, singleton handling and same-target agreement with a Python reference.

evidence.finding: Multiway FE/IV/GLM features, inference and performance comparison caveats.

projects.input: Unit/time identifiers, outcome, first-adoption cohort, comparison group, covariates and weighting/sampling design.
projects.output: ATT(g,t), influence functions and selected pointwise/uniform inference; aggregation requires appropriate retained influence information.
projects.assumptions: No anticipation, conditional group-specific parallel trends, comparison support and correct panel/repeated-cross-section interpretation.
projects.adapter_rule: Pinned att_gt allows at most one additional coarser cluster beyond individual ID. Uniform bands require bootstrap. compute_inffunc=False disables inference/pretests/bands and prevents aggte. Inspect fixed-weight anchor rules before using unbalanced panels.
projects.acceptance_test: Reproduce known cohort effects and weighted aggregations; reject incompatible changing-treatment encodings and unsupported cluster layouts. Explicitly test the points-only path cannot be promoted to an interval.

evidence.finding: att_gt design, weights, clustering, inference and aggregation controls.

projects.input: Event-study contrast vector, its full covariance, pre/post ordering, contrast weights and a specified trend-violation class.
projects.output: Restriction-dependent identified/confidence sets and a sensitivity curve.
projects.assumptions: The chosen restriction on post-treatment violations and the asymptotic approximation for input estimates hold.
projects.adapter_rule: Keep relative-magnitude and smoothness restrictions distinct, including time units and baseline normalization. Do not treat the worst observed pretrend as a known population bound.
projects.acceptance_test: Use a finite trend polytope with independently solved extrema, and known-covariance simulations for coverage; vary preperiod precision while holding the restriction fixed.

evidence.finding: Relative-magnitude/smoothness restrictions and inference accounting for pretrend estimation uncertainty.

projects.input: An outcome panel with controls/treated rows and untreated/treated time blocks under simultaneous adoption.
projects.output: Synthetic-DiD treatment contrast with method-specific uncertainty.
projects.assumptions: Block treatment layout, suitable donor/preperiod support and the method's outcome-model/design restrictions.
projects.adapter_rule: Reject staggered adoption as direct input to the documented block interface. Pin beta API and define aggregation before preprocessing.
projects.acceptance_test: Reproduce a rank-one factor panel with a known common treatment effect; reject mixed adoption dates and inspect donor-weight concentration.

evidence.finding: Simultaneous/block adoption, estimator/variance usage and beta status.

projects.input: Treated/control panel and an interactive-fixed-effect counterfactual model.
projects.output: Imputed untreated outcomes and their treatment contrasts.
projects.assumptions: Stable low-rank factor structure, sufficient untreated overlap, no relevant spillovers and justified extrapolation.
projects.adapter_rule: README states gsynth is now a fect wrapper maintained for backward compatibility. Qualify and pin fect separately before implementation. README 1.3.1 and DESCRIPTION 1.4.0 are distinct declarations, not interchangeable release evidence.
projects.acceptance_test: Use known low-rank factor panels and a treated-unit factor break; verify cross-validation excludes post-treatment leakage. Repeat against the actual pinned fect dependency.

evidence.finding: Interactive FE purpose, README version and fect/backward-compatibility notice.

projects.input: Episode-indexed state/action/reward/terminal data and a selected offline-RL model.
projects.output: Learned policy and value approximations under the learning objective.
projects.assumptions: Sufficient state/history, invariant reward/transition semantics, adequate behavior support and valid independent evaluation.
projects.adapter_rule: Separate policy fitting from causal identification and OPE; retain terminal/truncation distinction. Pin v2 API and training configuration. Distributed training does not establish policy-value coverage.
projects.acceptance_test: Train on a small known MDP, evaluate on independent trajectories, then remove an action from logging support; report unsupported policy choices instead of certifying them from Q-values.

evidence.finding: Offline/online APIs, v2 breaking changes, declared distributed training and supported algorithm table.

projects.input: Logged trajectories, behavior/target probabilities, horizon/discount and optional Q/occupancy nuisance estimates.
projects.output: Estimator-specific expected return, return distribution or policy-selection criterion with selected uncertainty routine.
projects.assumptions: Exchangeability/sufficient information, support, nuisance and sampling conditions for the chosen trajectory or marginal estimator.
projects.adapter_rule: Retain trajectory versus occupancy ratios and return-distribution versus mean targets. Interval-method availability does not establish coverage under hidden logging or arbitrary dependence.
projects.acceptance_test: Compare trajectory enumeration, IS and DR on a finite MDP; introduce a private logger and rare informative paths; assess bias and interval coverage by regime.

evidence.finding: Offline-RL workflow, trajectory/marginal/DR estimators, confidence routines and selection criteria.

projects.input: Context, logged action/reward, logging probability and target action distribution, including declared slate/position semantics.
projects.output: One-step policy value or contextual-bandit policy.
projects.assumptions: Bandit exchangeability/support and correct logging probabilities; slate models need their own reward/propensity factorization.
projects.adapter_rule: Do not route multi-period banking carryover to a contextual-bandit value. Preserve action/position conventions and evaluate learned policies on independent or appropriately split data.
projects.acceptance_test: Recover a one-step finite contextual value, then build a two-step carryover example showing that one-step reward can reverse the preferred policy.

evidence.finding: Bandit modules and supported standard/slate/continuous-action OPE families.

projects.input: Explicit transition/observation/reward model, initial belief and planner configuration.
projects.output: Model-conditional belief updates, simulated decisions and policy/planner outputs.
projects.assumptions: The supplied controlled model is valid for the intervention and the agent's available history; planner approximation is a separate numerical issue.
projects.adapter_rule: The inspected README qualifies a Python/Cython modeling/planning framework, not a causal parameter estimator. Inspect concrete planner and belief APIs before implementation; never pass smoothed future information as an online belief.
projects.acceptance_test: Compare a finite two-state belief update and short-horizon action values to exhaustive enumeration, then verify private logging changes observational filtering but not the intervention kernel.

evidence.finding: Framework to build and solve POMDPs; source-level role only.

projects.role: Julia POMDP interface and solver comparator
projects.input: State/action/observation spaces, initial law, transition, observation, reward and discount through the model interface.
projects.output: Solver-specific policy and model-conditional simulated/belief trajectories.
projects.assumptions: Controlled causal model and information filtration are already justified; solver approximations/guarantees depend on the separately chosen package.
projects.adapter_rule: Pin POMDPs.jl, POMDPTools, the solver and language bridge independently. The core interface does not itself implement all listed solvers. Keep pre/post-transition observation conventions explicit.
projects.acceptance_test: Use the same finite model across the project oracle and a pinned Julia solver; check observation indexing, discount timing and belief measurability.

evidence.finding: Core interface, separate tools/solvers, Tiger transition-observation-reward example.

projects.input: A specified likelihood/prior and observed/missing variables.
projects.output: Posterior draws or variational approximation and predictive quantities conditional on the model.
projects.assumptions: A properly defined probabilistic target, computational convergence/approximation and separately justified causal semantics.
projects.adapter_rule: Record likelihood factors and intervention transformation. pm.do/pm.observe syntax changes a supplied model; it does not establish that a bank's causal graph or latent mechanisms are identified.
projects.acceptance_test: Compare a conjugate posterior and a marginalized finite latent model to exact values; introduce observationally equivalent causal completions and verify prior sensitivity remains visible.

evidence.finding: MCMC/VI features and explicit do/observe example.

projects.input: A probabilistic program, observations, PRNG keys and inference configuration.
projects.output: MCMC/VI approximation to a specified posterior and diagnostics.
projects.assumptions: Target density and numerical conditions match the selected algorithm; latent marginalization or a valid mixed/discrete method is required where appropriate.
projects.adapter_rule: Do not claim all discrete states must be marginalized: the README documents MixedHMC and discrete VI as alternatives. Pin algorithm, precision, compiler, device and randomness. Fast differentiation does not identify interventions.
projects.acceptance_test: Compare exact finite-state marginalization and a conjugate continuous posterior; verify reproducible PRNG splitting and diagnose a difficult posterior rather than accepting speed alone.

evidence.finding: JAX substrate, HMC/NUTS, MixedHMC/discrete VI and divergence/reparameterization diagnostics.

projects.input: Discrete-time emission sequences, optional external inputs and initial/transition/emission parameter components.
projects.output: Conditional emission log likelihood, filtering/smoothing distributions and parameter-fitting ingredients.
projects.assumptions: The specified conditional-input SSM matches the observational experiment; treating adaptive actions as inputs requires a valid logger/conditioning argument.
projects.adapter_rule: HMM marginal_log_prob builds initial, transition and emission factors only. A private action likelihood is not supplied automatically. Standard transition components may ignore inputs; qualify the actual subclass and index mapping. Keep filtering separate from smoothing.
projects.acceptance_test: Compare finite latent-path summation to filter likelihood; include an informative private logger and demonstrate failure of a transition/emission-only likelihood. Verify input and observation timing explicitly.

evidence.finding: HMM law, optional input components, marginal_log_prob, filter, smoother and E-step.

projects.input: Versioned tables/files, explicit SQL and query configuration.
projects.output: Materialized histories/features or score sufficient-statistic reductions.
projects.assumptions: Keys, joins, event/availability semantics and aggregation preserve the declared population and information set.
projects.adapter_rule: Use SQL windows/nested types where useful but separately enforce time and cardinality contracts. No bank-scale throughput inferred from the README.
projects.acceptance_test: Backfill and duplicate-key adversaries; compare a materialized temporal join with exhaustive small-table enumeration and record peak memory/spill for the actual workload.

evidence.finding: SQL windows/nested types, clients and CSV/Parquet input.

projects.input: Versioned frames/files and a lazy/eager expression plan with selected engine.
projects.output: Transformed data/aggregates under query semantics.
projects.assumptions: Reordering, null handling, casts and time-zone/ordering semantics preserve the intended history and numerical result.
projects.adapter_rule: Retain the engine and physical plan; larger-than-memory and GPU declarations are capabilities to qualify, not causal-estimation speed evidence. Distributed cloud is not assumed to be the OSS execution path.
projects.acceptance_test: Require batch/streaming equivalence for ordered histories and cluster score sums within a declared tolerance; profile peak memory and unsupported-operation fallback.

evidence.finding: Lazy/eager engine, streaming, GPU and Arrow-interoperability declarations.

projects.input: An immutable partitioned dataset, task graph, model artifacts and deterministic fold/seed map.
projects.output: Distributed task results, fitted nuisance objects and reductions.
projects.assumptions: Statistical split boundaries and aggregation are invariant to scheduling, retries and worker count.
projects.adapter_rule: Adopt only after profiling. Tasks/actors/objects do not determine independent sampling units; retain explicit cluster/time partitioning and avoid duplicated score contributions on retry.
projects.acceptance_test: Kill/retry a worker during a bounded benchmark, change partition count, and require exactly-once logical contributions and equal fold membership; compare covariance with the local reference.

evidence.finding: Distributed runtime, AI libraries and task/actor/object abstractions.

projects.input: Catalog assets, ownership, schemas and lineage from bank systems.
projects.output: Searchable metadata graph and context for candidate data mappings.
projects.assumptions: Metadata completeness and semantic correctness are separate from causal assumptions and actual feature availability.
projects.adapter_rule: Use the existing enterprise catalog where possible. The README mixes OSS and Cloud capabilities: only its explicit OSS metadata-graph/lineage/governance/discovery declaration is relied on here. Human context proposals need evidence-backed field semantics.
projects.acceptance_test: Import a bounded synthetic asset graph, preserve stable IDs and source-version links, and ensure lineage edges cannot be promoted automatically to causal arrows.

evidence.finding: Explicit DataHub OSS versus Cloud capability distinction.

projects.input: Technical/business metadata, quality, ownership and lineage with stable asset identifiers.
projects.output: A unified metadata graph and schema-based context.
projects.assumptions: Catalog declarations may be incomplete or stale; technical lineage and business associations do not establish causal direction.
projects.adapter_rule: Integrate the bank's chosen catalog instead of requiring a second one. Qualify selected OSS connectors/API behavior before implementation; broad README capability lists are not an end-to-end test.
projects.acceptance_test: Reconcile a schema/ownership change and trace affected analysis inputs; retain unresolved definitions and verify no inferred adjustment set follows solely from catalog links.

evidence.finding: Metadata/quality/lineage/ownership/glossary/contracts graph declaration.
Schema-first collection/normalization architecture.

projects.input: Job/run/dataset identifiers and versioned event/facet payloads.
projects.output: Lineage events and an extensible provenance graph.
projects.assumptions: Emitted events are complete enough for replay and correspond to actual immutable data/model versions.
projects.adapter_rule: Define separate causal-analysis facets for target, observation clock, graph/model, split plan and estimator. A successful job event does not certify identification or inference.
projects.acceptance_test: Replay reordered/duplicate events, correlate one analysis to exact dataset/model artifacts, and require unknown facet versions to remain visible.

evidence.finding: Run/job/dataset model, runtime events and custom facets.

projects.input: Entity/event rows, feature references, TTL and optional created-timestamp filtering.
projects.output: A historical retrieval job whose features depend on timestamp configuration.
projects.assumptions: Configured event/creation timestamps represent the bank's actual decision information and source revision history.
projects.adapter_rule: The inspected API defaults filter_by_created_timestamp=False. Enabling it excludes later-created values only for views with created_timestamp_column. Require that field where availability matters and verify its business meaning; do not claim all Feast retrieval ignores availability time.
projects.acceptance_test: Use a feature dated before a decision but created after it. Check both flag settings, a missing creation field, TTL boundaries and revision tie-breaking against the declared history.

evidence.finding: Historical retrieval, event/TTL semantics, opt-in creation-time filter and unaffected views lacking the field.

projects.input: Record comparisons, blocking rules and a probabilistic linkage model.
projects.output: Pairwise match probabilities and thresholded/clustered candidate entity IDs.
projects.assumptions: Comparison-model calibration, blocking recall and dependence among fields; linkage uncertainty may depend on treatment/outcome.
projects.adapter_rule: Preserve match uncertainty and the linkage-data clock. A hard connected component is an estimated entity, not ground truth; avoid post-treatment features when defining baseline identities without justification.
projects.acceptance_test: Inject treatment-dependent false merges/splits and quantify their effect on the causal contrast; compare integration over candidate links with a hard-threshold analysis.

evidence.finding: Probabilistic linkage, Fellegi-Sunter basis, pair probabilities, clustering and highly correlated field limitation.

projects.input: Dataframe/schema and explicit type/value/cross-field checks.
projects.output: Validation result or schema failure.
projects.assumptions: The user-specified checks actually express the intended data contract; passing checks is not causal identification.
projects.adapter_rule: Use engine-specific schemas and preserve coercion/validation choices. Add product checks for unit keys, chronology and information availability; keep substantive assumptions distinct from executable checks.
projects.acceptance_test: Reject duplicated episode keys, wrong currency units and outcomes timestamped as baseline; include a valid-looking but confounded dataset to demonstrate the limit of schema validation.

evidence.finding: Multiple dataframe engines, schema/model APIs, custom checks and pandas import migration.

projects.input: Wide ordered treatment/covariate/outcome histories, a shift rule or shifted data, censoring/competing events, folds, sampling weights and optional cluster ID.
projects.output: TMLE/SDR policy mean, noncumulative density-ratio estimates and sequential regression fits.
projects.assumptions: Consistency, appropriate sequential exchangeability, support for the shifted law and adequate nuisance rates; finite memory k requires its own history-sufficiency argument.
projects.adapter_rule: Reject missing treatment under the documented capability matrix. Distinguish risk-ratio ipsi from odds tilting: at e=P(A=1|H), ipsi(delta) gives delta*e for delta<=1 and 1-(1-e)/delta for delta>1. Preserve mtp, shifted-overrides-shift and exact event/censoring interpretation.
projects.acceptance_test: For e=.2, delta=.5 gives .1 and delta=2 gives .6, versus odds-tilt values 1/9 and 1/3. Compare the declared policy mean to finite trajectory integration, including competing events and sampling weights.

evidence.finding: TMLE/SDR, risk-ratio incremental policies, missing-treatment limitation and competing risks.

projects.input: Wide data whose column order is causal time, binary treatment and censoring/event nodes, regime/rule and nuisance specifications.
projects.output: Regime mean or MSM projection, TMLE/IPTW (or G-computation), influence values and bounded/unbounded cumulative probabilities.
projects.assumptions: Sequential identification and censoring restrictions, regime support and estimator-specific regularity.
projects.adapter_rule: Validate chronology independently of column positions before constructing the input. Binary Anodes only; absorbing event coding must be coherent. projects.acceptance_test: Use finite-law g-formula/DR identities and a column permutation that would reverse chronology; require rejection before fitting. Show how outcome clipping and cumulative probability bounding change bias/target behavior.

evidence.finding: Column-order chronology, binary actions, absorbing survival events, outcome scaling/truncation and dynamic rules.

projects.input: Person-period data with explicit time, conditional covariate/outcome models, intervention functions, competing events, histories and Monte Carlo size.
projects.output: Intervention risks or terminal means/probabilities with model and optional bootstrap/simulation diagnostics.
projects.assumptions: Sequential g-formula identification, specified transition/outcome law and meaningful event/observation conventions.
projects.adapter_rule: Pin current intervention syntax; preserve baselags, visitprocess, competing-event handling and sim_trunc. sim_trunc defaults TRUE for specified continuous covariate families and alters the simulated law. nsimul controls Monte Carlo precision; nsamples controls bootstrap uncertainty.
projects.acceptance_test: Compare full-distribution simulation with exact two-period integration and mean-path substitution; vary nsimul separately from observed sample size. Use a tail-sensitive cash-flow target to quantify simulation truncation.

evidence.finding: Outcome-specific targets, conditional models, intervention API and baseline/history variables.
Visit process, competing events, lag convention, simulation/bootstrap controls and sim_trunc.

projects.input: Method-specific treatment/outcome/covariate data and explicitly selected weighting, g-computation, targeting or transport model.
projects.output: A specified point/longitudinal/transport estimand with that method's diagnostics.
projects.assumptions: Selected method's exchangeability, positivity, missingness and transport conditions.
projects.adapter_rule: Qualify individual classes before adapter implementation. The README documents monotone missingness for IPMW and single-time-point SNMM g-estimation; do not advertise general longitudinal SNMM fitting from the umbrella name.
projects.acceptance_test: Compare a chosen AIPW/g-computation class with an exact finite oracle, reject a nonmonotone pattern on a monotone-only path and distinguish point-treatment from longitudinal inputs.

evidence.finding: Specific g-method/transport features, monotone IPMW and single-time SNMM scope.

projects.input: Short panel, outcome lags, predetermined/exogenous regressors and explicit GMM/IV lag sets.
projects.output: Difference/system GMM coefficients, corrected two-step uncertainty and AR/Hansen diagnostics.
projects.assumptions: Lag orthogonality, serial-correlation and initial-condition restrictions; system moments require additional level restrictions.
projects.adapter_rule: Require an instrument ledger with count/lag depth/collapse choices. Automated model search and a nonrejected Hansen test do not establish valid moments or sufficient strength.
projects.acceptance_test: Compare sample moments to an independently built instrument matrix; add serial correlation and instrument proliferation; report bias and coverage alongside AR/Hansen output.

evidence.finding: Dynamic panel equation, GMM families, transformations, corrected SE, diagnostics and explicit command syntax.
